Codex 0.167.0 third-party notice candidate

Attribution scope -- Codex 0.167.0 private notice candidate

This collection maps the x86_64-pc-windows-msvc default-feature normal/build
source dependencies of codex-cli, codex-code-mode-host and codex-network-proxy.
Build dependencies are included. Source selection is not a per-executable link
map. Native source-tree notices and the producer full-lock inventory are
separate categories; retaining a notice does not assert every file is linked.

Earlier notice material is reused only for identical registry archive bytes
or an identical Git repository/revision/package identity. New source notice
bytes and original copyright lines are preserved. The two age crates' full
licenses were recovered at their published .cargo_vcs_info revisions and
checked against Git blob identities. No current-branch replacement was used.

deno_core_icudata 0.78.0 declares MIT but its exact source tree supplies no
copyright/license document. Standard MIT permission, conditions and disclaimer
are included without inventing an owner or year. The published author metadata
is not asserted copyright ownership. Its ICU data bytes exactly match the
pinned native ICU common/icudtl.dat; that component's notices are mapped too.
The unchanged debugserver-types and fxhash source-specific limitations remain
in their package observations; no missing owner attribution is manufactured.

Some files are license pointers or short grant headers. Retained observations
identify their exact-revision resolution. HPKE's Apache file is an attribution
header; its full MIT license and the full Apache text are both supplied here.
All original pointer/header bytes remain present.

Native material includes original licenses and selected glibc leading source
headers. The separate source downloads and practical native-to-host rebuild
proof address source/relink work. This notice archive alone is not a source
bundle, an official-binary reproduction or a legal conclusion. The native
producer full-lock source inventory has seven declaration-only mappings:
block 0.1.6; d3d12 0.4.1; dispatch 0.2.0; hexf-parse 0.2.1;
malloc_buf 0.0.6; objc_exception 0.1.2; ultraviolet 0.8.1.
Their exact published manifests declare the recorded license alternatives,
but a matching separate upstream copyright/license notice was not established.
Standard terms are supplied under declaration-only scope, without invented
owners/years or a claim of upstream notice recovery. Two lack published VCS
metadata; the exact five other repository roots supplied no separate license
file. Their original source archives remain unchanged. These limits are not
silently counted as missing selected-consumer notices or as legal clearance.
The two winapi GNU 0.4.0 packages also lack published VCS metadata, but their
exact published build.rs/src/lib.rs copyright and dual-license headers are
retained verbatim with standard full license terms. They are not owner-less
declaration-only mappings.

The mxc-sdk source delivery omits one unused 3,212,895-byte WSL nupkg under the
documented Windows default three-root selection. Preserve its upstream license,
the omitted-asset NOTICE/nuspec and projection scope with the source download.
Do not claim that projection covers targets/features which need the asset.

Final package integration, source-download availability and publication remain
separate checks. Original text files and source URLs are retained in this
archive; the displayed text may normalize its encoding, never its wording.

1,077 selected package mappings; 709 original text files.
T-numbers below refer to the complete text sections in this same file.

jpeg-encoder IJG License
========================

The jpeg-encoder crate declares license "(MIT OR Apache-2.0) AND IJG".
The published crate includes MIT and Apache license files, but it does not
currently include a top-level IJG license file. This Chromium-local file
documents the IJG terms for the IJG-derived portions of jpeg-encoder until the
crate publishes the missing license file upstream.

The IJG-derived portions include, at least:

- src/fdct.rs, which is ported from mozjpeg to Rust and states that it was part
  of the Independent JPEG Group's software.
- src/avx2/fdct.rs, which is ported from mozjpeg / jfdctint-avx2.asm to Rust
  and states that it is based on the x86 SIMD extension for the IJG JPEG
  library.

In the IJG terms below, "this software" refers to the IJG-derived portions of
jpeg-encoder listed above, not to the jpeg-encoder crate as a whole. The rest
of jpeg-encoder remains covered by the crate's MIT OR Apache-2.0 terms.

A. HISTORY OF THE SOFTWARE
==========================

Python was created in the early 1990s by Guido van Rossum at Stichting
Mathematisch Centrum (CWI, see http://www.cwi.nl) in the Netherlands
as a successor of a language called ABC.  Guido remains Python's
principal author, although it includes many contributions from others.

In 1995, Guido continued his work on Python at the Corporation for
National Research Initiatives (CNRI, see http://www.cnri.reston.va.us)
in Reston, Virginia where he released several versions of the
software.

In May 2000, Guido and the Python core development team moved to
BeOpen.com to form the BeOpen PythonLabs team.  In October of the same
year, the PythonLabs team moved to Digital Creations, which became
Zope Corporation.  In 2001, the Python Software Foundation (PSF, see
https://www.python.org/psf/) was formed, a non-profit organization
created specifically to own Python-related Intellectual Property.
Zope Corporation was a sponsoring member of the PSF.

All Python releases are Open Source (see http://www.opensource.org for
the Open Source Definition).  Historically, most, but not all, Python
releases have also been GPL-compatible; the table below summarizes
the various releases.

    Release         Derived     Year        Owner       GPL-
                    from                                compatible? (1)

    0.9.0 thru 1.2              1991-1995   CWI         yes
    1.3 thru 1.5.2  1.2         1995-1999   CNRI        yes
    1.6             1.5.2       2000        CNRI        no
    2.0             1.6         2000        BeOpen.com  no
    1.6.1           1.6         2001        CNRI        yes (2)
    2.1             2.0+1.6.1   2001        PSF         no
    2.0.1           2.0+1.6.1   2001        PSF         yes
    2.1.1           2.1+2.0.1   2001        PSF         yes
    2.1.2           2.1.1       2002        PSF         yes
    2.1.3           2.1.2       2002        PSF         yes
    2.2 and above   2.1.1       2001-now    PSF         yes

Footnotes:

(1) GPL-compatible doesn't mean that we're distributing Python under
    the GPL.  All Python licenses, unlike the GPL, let you distribute
    a modified version without making your changes open source.  The
    GPL-compatible licenses make it possible to combine Python with
    other software that is released under the GPL; the others don't.

(2) According to Richard Stallman, 1.6.1 is not GPL-compatible,
    because its license has a choice of law clause.  According to
    CNRI, however, Stallman's lawyer has told CNRI's lawyer that 1.6.1
    is "not incompatible" with the GPL.

Thanks to the many outside volunteers who have worked under Guido's
direction to make these releases possible.

Time Zone Database

  ICU uses the public domain data and code derived from Time Zone
Database for its time zone support. The ownership of the TZ database
is explained in BCP 175: Procedure for Maintaining the Time Zone
Database section 7.

 # 7.  Database Ownership
 #
 #    The TZ database itself is not an IETF Contribution or an IETF
 #    document.  Rather it is a pre-existing and regularly updated work
 #    that is in the public domain, and is intended to remain in the
 #    public domain.  Therefore, BCPs 78 [RFC5378] and 79 [RFC3979] do
 #    not apply to the TZ Database or contributions that individuals make
 #    to it.  Should any claims be made and substantiated against the TZ
 #    Database, the organization that is providing the IANA
 #    Considerations defined in this RFC, under the memorandum of
 #    understanding with the IETF, currently ICANN, may act in accordance
 #    with all competent court orders.  No ownership claims will be made
 #    by ICANN or the IETF Trust on the database or the code.  Any person
 #    making a contribution to the database or code waives all rights to
 #    future claims in that contribution or in the TZ Database.

PCRE LICENCE
------------

PCRE is a library of functions to support regular expressions whose syntax
and semantics are as close as possible to those of the Perl 5 language.

Release 7 of PCRE is distributed under the terms of the "BSD" licence, as
specified below. The documentation for PCRE, supplied in the "doc"
directory, is distributed under the same terms as the software itself.

The basic library functions are written in C and are freestanding. Also
included in the distribution is a set of C++ wrapper functions.
